title: InteractionConfig: the interaction block in every session home, the server interaction key and the front_model key
description: JSON Schema of WaaV's interaction configuration as published by W6 (W6-providers-endpoints.md section 3.10.7) under INTEGRATION_DECISIONS.md section 4, its Addenda A to D (A2 items 3 to 5 and 10, C5, C7.3, D5) and cross-check-consistency.md table 4.3. W1 to W7 name the seven workstreams, one per plan chapter: W1 runtime, W2 front model, W3 background tasks, W4 policy and human in the loop, W5 duplex audio, W6 providers and endpoints, W7 evaluation and rollout. The root validates the value a CLIENT sends as `interaction` (true, false or an object). $defs hold the server-side homes (alias, VoiceAgentEntry, RealtimeSettings, server defaults), the server `interaction` YAML key, the separate `front_model` key and the envelopes the examples use. The gateway parses leniently (InteractionConfig::from_json_lenient: a bad field keeps its default with config_warning interaction_value_ignored, an unknown key gives unknown_config_keys, a server-only key from a client gives interaction_override_refused); this schema is strict so that documents written for the plan are checked. Annotations: x-owner (workstream that owns the value), x-release (first release in which the path has an effect; 'lifecycle' for the Lifecycle track), x-access (who may set it: server_only, server_side_homes, operator_agent_homes (the server's interaction.defaults.agent and an agent-kind alias only), client, client_narrow, client_select, client_whitelist, client_operator_signed, client_names_only, client_within_clamps, client_lower_only, client_non_bud, client_ws_only), x-mid-session (true when interaction_update / bud.interaction.update may change it after the session starts). In Bud mode every client-settable path is additionally gated by the agent's session_overrides list (paths prefixed `interaction.`).

ClientInteractionSetting.description: The `interaction` value a client sends on /ws `config`, /realtime `config`, or inside a /v1/realtime patch. Absent means off and exactly today's behaviour; true means on with defaults.

ServerSideInteractionSetting.description: The `interaction` value in a server-side home: AliasDefinition.interaction, VoiceAgentEntry.interaction (budapp), RealtimeSettings.interaction (budapp), a DAG definition, and the server's interaction.defaults.agent / defaults.realtime blocks. Only the operator's agent homes (interaction.defaults.agent and an agent-kind alias) may carry `background`; the other homes use InteractionSettingWithoutAgentBackground.

InteractionSettingWithoutAgentBackground.description: A server-side `interaction` value that may not carry `background` (Addendum D5): budapp's VoiceAgentEntry.interaction (budapp declares the marker in the entry's own `background` block, VoiceAgentEntryProjection.background), budapp's RealtimeSettings.interaction and the server's defaults.realtime (realtime deployments are not Bud agent runs). The lenient parser ignores a `background` there with interaction_value_ignored.

ClientInteractionBlock.description: InteractionBlock minus the fields only server-side homes may set (speech.fallback) and the operator's agent declarations (background, Addendum D5); every other server-only field is already absent from InteractionBlock. A session sending either gets interaction_override_refused.

InteractionBlock.description: Server-only keys are not properties here and are refused from any session with interaction_override_refused: any `licence` key (the attestation lives only in front_model.licence), speech.truth_ack, allow_client_override, defaults, realtime_legacy_wire, duplex.compute (Addendum A2 item 5), the server task catalog under tasks (task_backends, allow_client_backends, allow_client_tools, allow_client_push, phone_continuation, speech_policy; A2 item 4), and any task backend URL, header or key. `background` (a Bud agent's answer marker, Addendum D5) is accepted only in the operator's agent homes and refused from any session with interaction_override_refused. Caller-memory and tenant-persona settings are not interaction keys: they live under front_model.memory and front_model.tenant_personas (A2 item 3, C5).

regime.description: A forced regime may only narrow (Addendum A2 item 7): it is honoured only when the provider can run it; the arms that force delegation (native client delegation, permanent native filler without exact speech, always-async tools without exact speech) are exclusive; auto owners resolve to provider in a forced delegating regime; otherwise, and on a cascade surface asked for another regime, the automatic choice is kept with config_warning regime_downgraded.

filler_owner.description: Who says acknowledgements and fillers. auto resolves per regime and provider (regime_resolve.py).

backchannel_owner.description: Who makes listening sounds while the caller talks.

idle_owner.description: Who prompts the caller after silence.

OperatorAgentBackground.x-owner: W6 (path and precedence), W3 (the marker rule)
OperatorAgentBackground.description: The operator's stand-in for budapp's VoiceAgentEntry.background.answer_marker (Addendum D5; W3 sections 3.13 and 3.17.2), so that a Bud agent known to emit the marker streams its answer sentence by sentence in Release 1 before budapp publishes the field (requested for 2026-11-02). Read from the server's interaction.defaults.agent (applies to the agents in interaction.defaults.agent_ids, or every agent when that list is empty) and from an agent-kind alias's interaction. An alias names no agent and the client picks it (handlers/ws/messages.rs:97-108), so the operator declares a marker there only when every agent that may be used with that alias emits it. Precedence, lowest to highest: server default, alias, budapp's own VoiceAgentEntry.background.answer_marker (which wins whenever present). Only answer_marker may be declared here: voice_approvals and side_runs remain the agent author's declarations in budapp (sign-offs 14 and 20). Refused from every session (interaction_override_refused); in any other home ignored with interaction_value_ignored. Without a marker a Bud agent's answer is relayed whole at completion, about 0.4 to 1 s later than today's agent path, and sign-off 13 accepts that explicitly.

answer_marker.description: The line the agent's prompt begins its final answer with (for example ANSWER:). Set: W3's rule marker (text before the marker is held as a draft and never spoken; each sentence after it is released as it completes). Null or absent: rule round_end, the whole response relayed at response.completed.

Speech.description: How the voice is chosen and how true it is. Effective from Release 3 (provider regimes); speech.realtime from Release 4. Never changeable mid-session.

voice_owner.description: gateway turns the provider into a half-cascade where half_cascade_possible (text output and a documented reply switch: only the OpenAI family, Addendum A2 item 1): the provider listens, WaaV decides every word and WaaV's text-to-speech is the voice; owners filler gateway, listening sounds none, idle gateway (A2 item 8). voice_owner_unavailable elsewhere.

voice_mismatch.description: May a gateway clip in a different voice read a confirmation (introduced by W4's template)? No sign-off number (W6 section 10 item 2).

truth.description: enforced limits the session to the cascade or half-cascade, else the session is refused (truth_enforcement_unavailable).

narrator.description: Regime B narrator: W4 templates, or the front model masked to the acts wait, progress and refuse.

clip_voice.description: Regimes B and C: the gateway clip voice; default the provider's voice when reproducible.

realtime.description: /ws only: run this session's voice on a realtime provider (regimes B and C on LiveKit and SIP).

fallback.description: Server-side homes only: the voice used when GPT-Live admission refuses (capacity_fallback).

channels.description: Where a question may be answered. [voice] on SIP-only sessions; dtmf only from Release 4.

attribution.description: source, kind, verbatim, act, task_id, utterance_id, chunk and heard on assistant_transcript

ga_mcp_approvals.description: /v1/realtime only: mirror confirm questions as GA mcp_approval_request items

Runtime.description: W1's runtime fields (W1 section 3.13). Removed: enabled, duck_on_bare_onset (now duplex.barge_in), answer_window_ms (now policy), front.breaker.* (W2's breaker only), idle.hangup_after_offer_ms (W4's agreed_wait_max_ms).

playback_lead_ms.description: default per transport: LiveKit 40, /ws 150, GA cascade 150

transport_lag_ms.description: default per transport: /ws 150, LiveKit 80, SIP 150, GA cascade 150

yield_backstop_ms.description: computed: W5's longest episode + 1,000 (about 7,700); a lower value is raised with a warning

Front.description: W2's block. Never a licence (front_model.licence is server-only), never persona text, bank lines, templates, protected terms or memory facts.

profile.description: auto (W2's resolution from its pinned qualified-profile list: lfm-standard, or lfm-large (LFM2.5-2.6B), when qualified and the server carries the licence attestation; else a qualified apache-standard (Qwen3.5-2B candidate); else scripted with front_model_scripted; Addendum B1 and B7: no profile is qualified in Release 1, so auto is scripted on every Release 1 deployment) or a name in front_model.profiles_enabled; a refused request gives front_profile_substituted.

persona.description: a registered persona id, optionally id@version; looked up in the session's tenant first, then the operator's

say_mode.description: free only with the server's free_text_ack

Caller.description: The four client-settable caller fields (INTEGRATION_DECISIONS.md section 7; the name field is preferred_name, Addendum C5) plus the operator-signed identity token, which is outside the whitelist (W6 section 3.20.2).

identity_token.description: Operator-signed caller identity in the one format W2 pins (W2 section 3.16.1; Addendum C5): v1.<payload>.<mac>, where payload is the unpadded base64url of the JSON object {sub (opaque caller id), tenant, exp (unix seconds, at most token_max_lifetime_s, default 300 s, ahead)} and mac is the unpadded base64url of HMAC-SHA-256 over "v1." + payload with a key derived from front_model.memory.identity_key_file. W2 verifies it and derives the keyed memory key; an invalid, expired or wrong-tenant token gives caller_identity_rejected and memory off for the session. The path and the warning code are W6's (Addendum A2 item 3).

Tasks.description: W3's block (W3 section 3.13). Backends are named, never given as URLs, headers or keys in a session.

default_backend.description: llm (conversation sessions), bud_agent (agent sessions), dag (DAG sessions), or a name from the operator catalog; provider sessions have no default (interaction_needs_background)

speculative_start.description: auto: on for the LLM tier, off for Bud, webhook, A2A, MCP, OpenAI Responses and DAG backends (sign-off 6). on for a backend that executes its own tools (budprompt, webhooks, A2A, MCP) is accepted only when the backend is declared free of side effects, else speculative_start_unsafe_backend (Addendum C2.2)

backends.description: names from the operator catalog this session may use

push_url.description: accepted from a client only when the operator sets allow_client_push

Policy.description: W4's PolicyConfig (W4 section 3.11); values outside the clamps are clamped with a config_warning; the effective block is echoed as policy_hash.

answer_window_ms.description: the one answer window, read by W1's interlock and W5's rule 5 (to be measured)

Duplex.description: W5's block (W5 section 3.11). compute is server-only (interaction.duplex.compute in the server key); a session sending it gets interaction_override_refused.

duck_on_bare_onset.description: moved here from W1's runtime block (INTEGRATION_DECISIONS.md section 4)

intensity.description: null: PersonaSpec.backchannel_intensity, else the transport default (web medium, phone off; sign-off 19); may only lower it

ServerInteractionKey.description: The one server `interaction` YAML key, parsed outside ServerConfig into InteractionServerConfig and stored in AppState (W1 owns the loader and the switch). Loaded from the same YAML file as ServerConfig; when ServerConfig came from the environment only, from WAAV_INTERACTION_* variables (Addendum C7.4). Never client-settable. Caller memory and tenant personas are configured under front_model, not here (Addendum A2 item 3).

enabled.description: the operator switch; WAAV_INTERACTION_ENABLED mirrors it; when false a session's interaction gives interaction_disabled_by_server

truth_ack.description: providers ('provider' or 'provider:model') the operator accepts with monitored truth; regimes B and C are refused (truth_ack_required) for any other (sign-off 10)

agent.description: operator default for Bud agent sessions (sign-off 13); may carry background.answer_marker for agents the operator knows emit the marker (Addendum D5); budapp's VoiceAgentEntry.interaction and VoiceAgentEntry.background win when present

realtime.description: operator default for Bud realtime deployments, like defaults.agent (Addendum C7.3); budapp's RealtimeSettings.interaction wins when present

allow_client_override.description: dotted paths /v1/realtime clients may set through bud.interaction.update

realtime_legacy_wire.description: escape flags restoring today's wire for non-Bud sessions (W6 section 9.2); Bud deployments use RealtimeSettings.policy.legacy_wire

compute.description: W5's analyser compute pool: server-only (Addendum A2 item 5); refused from every session

ServerTasks.description: W3's operator catalog and switches, under interaction.tasks.* (Addendum A2 item 4: W3 renames task_backends, allow_client_backends, allow_client_tools, allow_client_push, phone_continuation and speech_policy under it). Server-only: a session sending any of them gets interaction_override_refused.

FrontModelKey.description: W2's separate server key (W2 section 3.13). Built dark in Release 0. Carries the licence attestation of INTEGRATION_DECISIONS.md section 2.1 and, from Release 2, the caller-memory and tenant-persona settings (Addendum A2 item 3 and C5). Profile qualification is not configuration: it comes from W2's pinned qualified-profile list shipped with the gateway (empty in Release 1, Addendum B1).

profile.description: auto, or a profile the operator forces for evaluation (lfm-standard, lfm-large, apache-standard, scripted); an unqualified profile runs only with allow_unqualified (echoed qualified: false)

licence.description: the operator attests its legal entity (with affiliates) is under the LFM Open License threshold, or holds a Liquid commercial licence; env WAAV_FRONT_LICENCE; required to run any LFM profile; echoed as an attestation kind only

allow_unqualified.description: lets an explicitly named profile run although W2's qualified-profile list does not include it (Release 1 evaluation; sign-off 4: CI forces the Qwen3.5-2B candidate this way)

memory.x-owner: W2 (store, token format), W6 (session path and warning)
memory.description: caller memory, off by default (sign-off 16; W2 section 3.16; Addendum A2 item 3 and C5). The session carries interaction.front.caller.identity_token; an invalid token gives caller_identity_rejected; memory enabled while the task store runs in its in-memory fallback gives caller_memory_unavailable.

identity_key_file.description: required when enabled: the key that checks the token's MAC and derives the keyed memory key

tenant_personas.description: the tenant persona registration route PUT /v1/interaction/personas/{id} (sign-off 17; W2 section 3.17; Addendum C5): mounted only when the interaction switch and enabled are on, and only with the task Redis

AliasDefinition.description: AliasDefinition (core/alias/mod.rs:150-171, deny_unknown_fields) plus the new interaction field. An alias that sets only kind and interaction (an interaction-only alias) may combine with agent; one that sets stt, tts, llm or dag_template is still refused with agent (handlers/ws/config_handler.rs:840-842). An agent-kind alias may declare interaction.background.answer_marker (Addendum D5); in an alias of another kind it is ignored with interaction_value_ignored.

ServerConfigDocument.description: The parts of the server YAML (written as JSON) that carry interaction settings: the interaction key, the front_model key and aliases. Other server keys are allowed and not described.

WsConfigEnvelope.description: The /ws `config` message (handlers/ws/messages.rs:49-109) with the new top-level interaction field (protocol 1.1). Existing fields are not re-described here.

RealtimeConfigEnvelope.description: The /realtime `config` message (RealtimeSessionConfig) with interaction (Release 3). interaction is accepted only on config, never on update_session.

model_family.description: Azure only (Addendum A2 item 10): the model family behind the deployment named in model (for example gpt-realtime-2.1), so the preamble and lifecycle rules can be evaluated. Unset: fillers resolve to gateway and an interaction session gets model_family_unknown. A Bud deployment sets it in RealtimeSettings.

VoiceAgentEntryProjection.description: Excerpt of budapp's VoiceAgentEntry projection (bud-auth/src/voice_agent.rs; budapp is the single writer, :3) with the new interaction and background fields. Unknown top-level fields are already accepted and logged (KNOWN_FIELDS, :332-353; the check at :405-409), so budapp can publish both before WaaV reads them. Requested dates (cross-team, Addendum D5 and the plan): interaction and background.answer_marker for Release 1 by 2026-11-02; background.voice_approvals and background.side_runs for Release 2 by 2026-11-30. Other entry fields are allowed and not described.

AgentBackground.description: budapp's background block on the agent entry (W3 section 3.13). Only the agent's author can make these declarations; the operator may stand in for answer_marker alone (OperatorAgentBackground, Addendum D5), and this field wins over the operator's.

mode.description: auto: a background run when budprompt allows it

voice_approvals.description: invoker: the caller's spoken vote may be forwarded (sign-off 14)

side_runs.description: concurrent runs without the conversation are safe for this agent (sign-off 20)

RealtimeSettingsProjection.description: Excerpt of budapp's deployment RealtimeSettings (bud-auth/src/endpoint_config.rs:299) with the new interaction field (Release 3 for the relay and facade; budapp's fields requested by 2027-03-12) and the per-deployment escape flags of W6 section 9.2. Other fields are allowed and not described.

BudInteractionUpdate.description: /v1/realtime client event bud.interaction.update; intercepted before the relay policy; only paths in the agent's session_overrides (cascade) or the server's allow_client_override (relay and facade) are applied; answer bud.interaction.updated {applied, refused}.
